description: A.S.F.R.E.E release, source-of-truth and compatibility-routing governance acceptance specifications. These are specifications until run in a real harness. Includes registry uniqueness, canonical version authority, redirect migration and fail-closed cases.

cases.input: The repository plugin package, compatibility manifest, app-backed release and local runtime use different version identifiers.
cases.expected: The package manifest is authoritative for package SemVer; compatibility manifest and package README match it; Plugin Creator is independently updated and read back; runtime and bundle versions remain separate.
cases.must_not: Do not equate plugin, runtime, bundle, or legacy redirect versions.

cases.input: A request arrives through a historical unnumbered skill name such as artifact-intelligence.
cases.expected: Resolve the alias to exactly one numbered O01–O12 canonical skill; the alias carries no independent workflow, state, or authority.
cases.must_not: Do not invoke both the alias and canonical skill as separate specialists or revive stale duplicated instructions.

cases.input: A reviewed repository package is updated but the Plugin Creator release has not yet been updated.
cases.expected: Report repository source update and app deployment as separate lifecycle states; after app update, verify release metadata and file read-back against the reviewed source.
cases.must_not: Do not claim the installed app is updated because a GitHub commit or PR exists.

cases.input: A README links to runtime/README.md while the repository stores the runtime as checksum-pinned source bundles reconstructed by scripts.
cases.expected: Link to a tracked runtime reproduction guide; identify the runtime workspace as generated after extraction and overlays.
cases.must_not: Do not imply runtime/ is checked in or claim the source bundle is an active deployed service.

cases.input: The two manifests, README version, compatibility skill folders, or alias destinations drift from the release governance contract.
cases.expected: Static validation fails with a specific error before package release.
cases.must_not: Do not silently accept manifest divergence, unregistered skill folders, or duplicated alias procedures.

cases.input: A product has two Plugin Creator packages both claiming to be its canonical orchestrator.
cases.expected: The registry admits exactly one CANONICAL plugin for the product_id; every other package must have a distinct registered role and identity.
cases.must_not: Do not allow a second master orchestrator or choose a canonical package by display-name similarity.

cases.input: Two registry entries reuse a plugin_id, identity_id or plugin_name.
cases.expected: Static validation rejects the duplicate identity before release.
cases.must_not: Do not resolve collisions by silently renaming, overwriting or reassigning an existing plugin identity.

cases.input: The legacy redirect package has its own version while the canonical product package has a different SemVer.
cases.expected: Each version is resolved only from its declared source; redirect SemVer identifies the redirect shell and never pins canonical product version.
cases.must_not: Do not numerically compare or synchronize unrelated package/runtime/bundle/redirect version planes.

cases.input: A pull request or release candidate contains a higher package version than the currently merged main branch.
cases.expected: Keep the merged main-branch version as active until review and merge complete; app deployment/read-back is a separate subsequent gate.
cases.must_not: Do not report PR_OPEN or an uploaded archive as an active RELEASED/DEPLOYED state.

cases.input: A legacy record contains an unknown enum or a status whose meaning differs from a canonical status.
cases.expected: Reject or quarantine the value, preserve provenance and map only semantically equivalent values through the documented migration table.
cases.must_not: Do not coerce unknown or semantically different values to the nearest-looking canonical enum.

cases.input: The canonical plugin cannot be opened, or a user expects the legacy package to transfer chat history and files automatically.
cases.expected: Report the canonical destination as unavailable and stop; explain that context/files require a deliberate manual migration and evidence revalidation.
cases.must_not: Do not revive legacy behavior, claim automatic memory/chat migration, or copy secrets into the new context.
